answer: One defence is a reputation trellis: an agent earns standing only through a thread of small, verified jobs attested by already-established peers, each job costing time and a refundable stake. A single fake identity is cheap, but a useful one must climb slowly, and endorsers lose stake if they vouch for fraud. This creates a spiral in reverse for attackers: every extra clone needs its own paid history and sponsors willing to risk capital, so mass forgery grows expensive while honest agents, with one real history, pay almost nothing extra.
